title: Alloy: scopes and instances
objective: Judge what a bounded check at a scope establishes beside other kinds of result, find a world within a scope, and tell a subset constraint that holds only vacuously.

blocks.md:
`run` asks Alloy for an instance that satisfies a predicate within a scope. `check` asks for a counterexample to an assertion within a scope. A check that finds none says nothing beyond its scope: MODEL-CHECKED [M], with the scope, complete within it.

A check over a contradictory model passes vacuously, the same trap as an `unsat` without a premise witness (D-02), so pair every `check` with a satisfiable `run`.

Daniel Jackson's argument is that many bugs have small counterexamples, so bounded analysis raises no false alarms but cannot prove anything. It is a hypothesis about where bugs usually live, not a theorem about every size.
`s in t` says s is a subset of t, and on an empty s it holds vacuously. Overlap is `some s & t`.

Alloy runs on the Bench, optionally {{run:RUN-alloy-version}}. Alloy4Fun is a disclosed, uncredited link-out only, because it stores models on its server. The tab has no Alloy, so this drawer's items are keyed by Z3 and the Datalog engine over finite worlds.

RUN-alloy-version.title: Alloy 6.2.0: its version and a headless smoke run

values.java: OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM Temurin-21.0.12.1+1 (build 21.0.12.1+1-LTS, mixed mode, sharing)

notes: Alloy 6.2.0 is optional and used only by drawer D-16 (spine section 9.2). It needs Java 17 or later; this run uses the Bench base image, Eclipse Temurin 21.
The release asset org.alloytools.alloy.dist.jar publishes no checksum, so it is pinned by the SHA-256 measured here. A later download that differs is unpinned, whatever its name says.

The smoke model is two commands: the run finds an instance (SAT) and the check of the assertion has none (UNSAT). Both are bounded by their scopes (3 and 4 atoms), so the check is bounded evidence, never a proof.

exec prints its verdict lines on standard error and overwrites a progress counter with backspaces; verdict_lines holds standard error first, then standard output (which is empty), with each line as a terminal shows it.
receipt.json and the solution file hold timestamps and durations, so a re-run is compared on verdict_lines only.
The run used eclipse-temurin:21-jre with the network off; the jar was mounted read-only.
